description: Bumping the Spring Boot BOM line while the version catalog pins an older junit-bom detonates the test executor at DISCOVERY, not compile: the Boot BOM force-upgrades junit-platform-engine but Gradle 8.x auto-loads junit-platform-launcher from its own distribution (older), and the unaligned pair dies with 'OutputDirectoryProvider not available' / 'TestEngine junit-jupiter failed to discover tests' — an executor-level crash with no failing testcase, easy to misread as a module problem. Only modules importing the Boot BOM crash; Spring-free modules (core) stay green, which misdirects triage.
resolution: Two-part fix, both Gradle-9-required anyway: (1) align the catalog junit pin with the Boot BOM's managed Jupiter version (resolve via :module:dependencies --configuration testRuntimeClasspath); (2) declare testRuntimeOnly 'org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher' in EVERY test-bearing module so the launcher resolves from the same BOM as the engine — this also deletes the 'Deprecated Gradle features ... incompatible with Gradle 9.0' warning (Gradle 9 removes launcher auto-loading entirely). Diagnose executor-level crashes from the JUnit XML failure CAUSE CHAIN (Caused by lines), not the report summary.

description: Porting to Framework 7 / Boot 4 silently kills OTEL-agent trace attribution: the opentelemetry javaagent 2.11.0 baked into the catalog image emits ZERO spans on the new stack (its spring-webmvc/tomcat instrumentation predates Framework 7), so the load harness's amplification step finds '0 attributable traces — refusing to extrapolate' while everything else looks healthy. Also two harness limits only a FASTER stack exposes: (1) the ceiling ladder outlives one ~5-min access token once no early knee stops it (stale-token 401s RED an otherwise valid climb); (2) when OPA collapses under compile+bulk load the app answers fail-closed EMPTY pages (200, fast, count=0) — invisible to a knee rule keyed on p99/failed%, so wrong_count REDs the run instead of declaring the real knee (an OPA-availability cliff).
resolution: Bump the agent with the stack (2.29.0 works on Framework 7) and prove traces flow with a 1-request smoke against Jaeger BEFORE burning k6 time. Re-mint the perf token per ladder stage (surgical, validity-preserving — auth is never the measured quantity). Treat the fail-closed-empty-page knee blindness as an ADR-0021 methodology decision, not a quick patch — record the cliff honestly in the ledger and defer the knee-definition change. Also: deploy.sh build rebuilds ONLY the catalog image; usermgmt builds lazily IF MISSING — always verify BOTH images' created-at before trusting a fleet run.

name: Boot 4 port: the churn is modularization, not APIs — locate classes in jars, never guess packages
description: Porting Boot 3.5 -> 4.0 the dominant breakage class is Boot's split of spring-boot/spring-boot-autoconfigure/spring-boot-test into per-technology artifacts. Three distinct symptoms map to it: (1) compile 'package does not exist' (class moved artifact AND sometimes package: TestRestTemplate -> org.springframework.boot.resttestclient in spring-boot-resttestclient; DataJpaTest -> spring-boot-data-jpa-test; AutoConfigureMockMvc -> spring-boot-webmvc-test; EntityScan -> spring-boot-persistence; ClientHttpRequestFactoryBuilder kept its package but moved to spring-boot-http-client, its Settings type renamed HttpClientSettings). (2) runtime auto-config silently absent (liquibase-core on classpath but LiquibaseAutoConfiguration lives in spring-boot-liquibase -> no migration runs -> ddl-auto:validate fails 'missing table' — looks like a Hibernate 7 problem, is a missing-artifact problem). (3) test auto-config 'Failed to introspect Class' (spring-boot-resttestclient references RestTemplateBuilder from spring-boot-restclient as an OPTIONAL dep — add it explicitly). Also: @SpringBootTest no longer auto-provides TestRestTemplate — @AutoConfigureTestRestTemplate goes on RANDOM_PORT bases only (on a MOCK-env base it fails 'No local test web server available'). Working method that converged in 12 iterations with zero wrong turns: run the build, take the FIRST error, locate the class in the resolved Boot BOM artifacts (unzip -l over ~/.gradle/caches, or fetch the jar from Central) with javap for exact signatures, fix, rebuild. The Boot BOM POM (spring-boot-dependencies) is the authoritative artifact directory. Also Framework 7 renames HttpStatus.resolve(422) to UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT (equality asserts on the UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY alias break; wire bytes identical).

Swapping a library to Jackson 3 (tools.jackson) breaks Hibernate 7.2 jsonb boot in every downstream JPA context: Hibernate's JSON FormatMapper (required at EntityManagerFactory creation once ANY @JdbcTypeCode(SqlTypes.JSON) attribute exists in the model) probes ONLY com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper — Hibernate ORM 7.2 has no tools.jackson support (verified via javap on org.hibernate.type.format.jackson.JacksonIntegration). The failure ('Could not find a FormatMapper for the JSON format') appears only AFTER the last Jackson-2 databind leaves the classpath, so a staged migration masks it until the final module swaps.
resolution: Keep Jackson 2 solely as Hibernate's internal JSON engine: runtimeOnly('com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind') on the JPA module (Boot 4's BOM still manages the jackson-2 line — 2.21.4 — precisely for this). Zero com.fasterxml databind types in source; grep-clean stays achievable. Do NOT ship a custom Jackson-3 FormatMapper for a mechanical port — new public surface for something upstream will obsolete. Drop the runtimeOnly when Hibernate ORM gains Jackson 3 support. Also Jackson 3 API deltas worth knowing: JsonNode.fieldNames() -> propertyNames() returning Collection (AssertJ .toIterable() bridges die), JsonProcessingException -> unchecked tools.jackson.core.JacksonException, java.time ISO-8601 built in (JavaTimeModule ceremony deleted).

name: Spring AI 2.0.0 MCP server runs on Boot 4.0.7 (and must exclude opa-abac-spring-data)
description: Adding example-mcp-server (Phase 9 T1) hit two dependency facts worth not re-deriving. (1) VERSION SKEW IS BENIGN: spring-ai-starter-mcp-server-webmvc:2.0.0's POM declares spring-boot 4.1.0, but the io.spring.dependency-management plugin imports THIS repo's Boot BOM (4.0.7 via libs.versions.toml) first, so every spring-boot-* artifact resolves to 4.0.7. Verified empirically before writing any T1 code with a throwaway context-start spike: the MCP auto-configuration registers 15 beans (McpServerSseWebMvcAutoConfiguration + McpServerAnnotationScannerAutoConfiguration + mcpSyncServer) and the context starts clean. Do NOT bump the repo to Boot 4.1.x for Spring AI's sake - that is a separate slice. (2) THE STARTER DRAGS JPA: opa-abac-spring-boot-starter api-depends on opa-abac-spring-data, which api-depends on spring-boot-starter-data-jpa. Any adopter module WITHOUT persistence therefore gets DataSource auto-configuration and dies at startup with 'Failed to determine a suitable driver class'. Fix is exclude(group='dev.dmitriikonovalov', module='opa-abac-spring-data') on the starter dependency, so the JPA auto-configs back off on an ABSENT classpath rather than being disabled by name - this is the 'depend on what you use' path the starter's own build.gradle.kts documents for non-web/non-JPA adopters. Annotation coordinates for the record: @McpTool/@McpToolParam are org.springframework.ai.mcp.annotation.* (Spring AI's, NOT the io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk group, which ships no annotations artifact in 2.0.0).

McpServerProperties.protocol has field default STREAMABLE, but the auto-config @Conditionals in spring-ai-autoconfigure-mcp-server-common match on the PROPERTY STRING, not the bound field: with spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol absent, EnabledSseServerCondition wins and the app serves WebMvcSseServerTransportProvider (GET /sse + POST /mcp/message) while POST /mcp returns 404. Verified 2026-07-29 by javap of the 2.0.0 jars + a live boot in the spring-ai-mcp-hello lab (~/Workspace/ai-engineering/spring-ai-mcp-hello). CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS REPO: example-mcp-server application.yml sets no protocol, so the T1-T4 module actually runs the SSE transport despite the design/docs saying streamable-HTTP; McpServerSecurityTest never caught it because security returns 401/403 before routing. T6 (or the T5 design amendment) must set spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol: STREAMABLE explicitly and the e2e client must speak streamable framing (responses may be plain application/json for initialize but SSE-framed text/event-stream for tools/list on the same endpoint).
resolution: Always set spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol explicitly (STREAMABLE for /mcp); assert transport routing in a test that bypasses/authenticates through security rather than reading a 401 as proof the endpoint exists.

name: MCP SDK 2.0.0 roster-adapter pins + the two traps (delete at java-sdk #578)
description: VERIFIED by javap + a working lab spike 2026-07-31. THE REFLECTIVE ROUTE to filter tools/list per caller (no supported seam exists at 2.0.0): resolve the transport provider by INTERFACE type io.modelcontextprotocol.spec.McpStreamableServerTransportProvider -> private field "sessionFactory" -> cast to the PUBLIC io.modelcontextprotocol.spec.DefaultMcpStreamableServerSessionFactory -> its PACKAGE-PRIVATE field "requestHandlers" (Map<String, McpRequestHandler<?>>). Two setAccessible reads, no third hop; both jars are non-modular so no --add-opens. Wrap the "tools/list" entry once at startup (SmartInitializingSingleton, before the connector opens); the map is SHARED by every session, so one put covers all callers, and it must never be mutated after traffic starts (plain HashMap). Observed live: the map holds 10 handlers - prompts/get, resources/templates/list, ping, prompts/list, resources/read, completion/complete, tools/call, resources/list, logging/setLevel, tools/list. TRAP 1: McpSchema.ListToolsResult is a RECORD carrying (tools, nextCursor, meta) and its only builder is builder(List<Tool>) - rebuilding via builder(kept).build() SILENTLY DROPS nextCursor and meta; use the full 3-arg constructor. TRAP 2: spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol must be set EXPLICITLY to STREAMABLE - the auto-config @Conditionals match the property string with matchIfMissing=true on SSE, ignoring the properties-field default of STREAMABLE, so an absent property serves the legacy deprecated SSE transport (GET /sse + POST /mcp/message) and POST /mcp 404s. DELETION TRIGGER: java-sdk #578 (pluggable ToolsRepository with per-request context, targeted at an opt-in 2.1) - when it ships, delete the installer and reimplement against the supported seam; the filter core and its tests survive untouched. Working reference implementation: spring-ai-mcp-hello/src/main/java/.../RosterFilterSpike.java (throwaway lab, filters by hardcoded name rather than policy).
